question: Should OpenClaw Core own a durable Pi/Review/git-promotion orchestration boundary, or should this remain outside Core behind an explicitly supported extension/service contract?
rationale: The patch introduces a new product and ownership boundary across external services; choosing the permanent Core-versus-service contract cannot be resolved mechanically from this branch.

options.title: Keep orchestration outside Core
options.body: Reject the Core-owned implementation and require the external services to own their coordination until a supported generic extension seam is designed.

options.title: Sponsor a Core boundary
options.body: Approve a narrowly defined Core orchestration contract, then require repository-contained fixtures, dependency approval, and upgrade/security proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep orchestration outside Core
recommendation.body: Reject the Core-owned implementation and require the external services to own their coordination until a supported generic extension seam is designed.

likelyOwner.reason: TaskFlow is the persistence boundary the proposed feature extends, so its current owners are the closest available routing candidates.
